News.title: Chilling rise of ‘violence-to-order’ group across Europe with teens hired to carry out hits & rape victims for £1.8k
News.content:
A NEW message lights up hundreds of phones across the world as members of a sick group chat are alerted to a list of services – contract killings, arson attacks, torture and rape, all being offered for a price.

The messaging network is known as violence-as-a-service or VAAS, and in an incredible sinsiter twist, crime gangs are now using them to recruit teens who are willing to carry out their dirty work throughout Europe for thousands of pounds.





Experts also told The Sun how this rapidly evolving threat could easily be exploited by countries like Russia and Iran seeking to build an army of vulnerable youngsters to unleash bloodshed on their enemies.

Telegram has emerged as a popular platform for criminals offering VAAS.

Gangs post messages such as, “services available in any country”, and “anywhere can get done at any time”, accompanied by a series of gun, death and bomb emojis.

One active group, Kirk Mafia, which claimed responsibility for an arson attack just weeks ago, advertises hits across the US, UK and Canada with prices starting at $2,500 (£1,800).

Services listed to its 799 subscribers include bricking, arson and shootings.

Within the chat, some users actively seek out services to order, with one writing: “How much are bricking services in the UK”.

The group – named after US President Donald Trump‘s ally Charlie Kirk who was fatally shot in September – emerged as a swatting service.

It claims to have triggered more than 30 swats – spoofing emergency calls to spark high-intensity law enforcement responses – since February 2026.





But recently, the network has turned to more aggressive tactics.

Expert on violent extremism, Mia Bloom, told The Sun that Telegram’s lax security measures act as an “echo chamber” for criminal groups.

The platform, which hosts more than one billion users, was built with end-to-end encryption and features that prioritise user privacy.

Bloom said: “Telegram draws in like-minded individuals, allowing them to congregate in channels sharing hate.

“There’s a lack of moderation. In fact, criminals and extremists often moderate their own channels – vetting and blocking accounts to ensure their chats haven’t been infiltrated by law enforcement.”

Kirk Mafia appears to be part of a growing trend of swatting groups turning to violence in a chilling new gig economy.

Other sick groups go as far as to inflict rape, shootings and beatings that promise to leave victims with broken bones and coughing up blood for cash.

It remains unclear how many of the adverts seen by The Sun may be genuine offers or scams.



But last year, Europol arrested nearly 200 people, including minors, for VAAS-related offences in just six months.

Dubbed GRIMM, the force is a collaboration between Europol and 11 European countries aimed at countering the surge.

Marking its first year in operation last month, Europol announced a total of 280 arrests – including six “high-value targets”.

Across its investigation, 14,000 accounts linked to VAAS were identified.

Europol said in a statement: “These figures point to a fundamental shift in how violence is organised and deployed.

“Violence is no longer confined to isolated acts or local dynamics.

“It is increasingly offered as a service: accessible, scalable and driven by online ecosystems that enable recruitment, coordination, and execution across borders.”

The team works across Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the UK.

During its first six months, GRIMM arrested 63 people directly involved in carrying out or planning violent crimes and 40 “enablers” accused of facilitating violence-for-hire services.

An additional 84 recruiters were cuffed, as well as six “instigators”.



The separate roles allow criminals to “operate like an outsourced service”, making it harder to track crimes back to the ring leaders.

Among the suspects arrested was a Dutch national accused of being a getaway driver for two minors allegedly responsible for a string of explosions in Germany in July and August 2025.

And seven people aged 14 to 26 were arrested in Denmark for allegedly using messaging apps to hire other teens for contract killings.

In a chilling twist, Europol revealed that those carrying out the violent attacks are often youngsters without a criminal record.

The agency said: “Social media platforms and messaging apps are used to reach young people through coded language, memes, and gamified tasks.”

In return for money, “status or a sense of belonging”, vulnerable young people are drawn into “violent” criminal schemes.

VAAS is believed to have spawned from Sweden, which is currently experiencing a wave of brutal gang violence, but the phenomenon is now spreading across the world at a terrifying pace.



Cybersecurity company Trend Micro uncovered criminals offering to carry out brutal attacks for the highest bidder on online forums in Russia.

Users offered to commit “grievous bodily harm” for $5,000 (£3,700), while “torture with extortion of information” was on sale for $6,000 (£4,500) and arson of a target’s apartment was priced at $10,000 (£7,500).

Steven Rai, extremism analyst at the Institute for Strategic Dialogue, told The Sun this “thriving market” could easily be scaled up for state violence.

He said: “VAAS lowers the barrier to violence by allowing buyers and attackers to connect across borders without ever meeting in person.

“What raises the stakes even further is not simply the individual acts of violence, but the scalability of this model.

“VAAS has been understood as a criminal market in which lone or organised criminals advertise harmful services in exchange for financial rewards.

“But we have recently seen governments like Russia and Iran manipulating these markets.”

Steven said this “significantly ups the ante” for the scale of violence being ordered and carried out online.



Young people are willing to sell themselves as “disposable operatives for state violence”.

“Even when they do not fully understand who is directing or benefiting from their actions”, he added.

It comes after two Russian-linked men in their 20s were found guilty of conspiring to carry out arson attacks on property linked to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

The pair had been acting on the orders of a Russian-speaking Telegram contact known as “El Money” who recruited them to carry out the attacks for cash.

The Russian-speaking mastermind behind the attacks aimed cause “unrest” across the country, said commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) London.

To tackle this growing threat, Steven said authorities must share information across borders and introduce “consistent pressure on the platforms that allow it.”

Steven said: “At the same time, preventing violence from occurring – rather than merely responding to it – is also essential.

“Many recruits appear to be young people drawn in by money or the possibility of obtaining status, so early intervention is critical to preventing real-world harm.”

A Telegram spokesperson told The Sun that calls to violence are “explicitly forbidden” on its platform.

Users who break its terms of service are “routinely removed by moderators” to keep the platform safe, the spokesperson added.

News.title: Man dies after plunging 100ft from cliff top onto busy beach during heatwave in front of horrified onlookers
News.content:
BEACH FALL Man dies after plunging 100ft from cliff top onto busy beach during heatwave in front of horrified onlookers

A MAN has tragically died after falling 100ft from a clifftop road in a shocking incident.

Onlookers were traumatised by the “terrifying” moment they saw him plunge onto the beach.





Cops yesterday responded to a report of “concern for welfare” of a man near Boscombe beach in Bournemouth.

Dorset Police confirmed its officers had found and spoken to the man, adding “it was subsequently reported that he has fallen from height”.

In the hot and sunny weather, the sandy beach was packed with people who flocked to the seaside.

One eyewitness was on the beach just in front of the area where he fell, telling Dorset Echo: “I was on the beach directly opposite, getting myself organised and I looked up and saw movement.”



They said they saw the man atop the cliff seconds before he fell, adding the sight was “terrifying” and “very, very sad”.

From further along the beach, another eyewitness said the incident was “horrible”.

They said the man had been stood on top of the Fisherman’s Walk Cliff Lift before he fell.

Another person nearby said “there were loads of people crying” after the tragic fall.



The force urged members of the public “not to share images and videos of the incident online”.

After his death, a Dorset Police spokesperson said: “The man is yet to be formally identified.

“The death is not being treated as suspicious and a file will be prepared for HM Coroner.

“As police were already in attendance when the fall happened, a referral was made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) as is standard in incidents of this nature.”

A police cordon was set up and much of the beach cleared to make way for the air ambulance which rushed to the scene.



Multiple emergency vehicles scrambled to the scene, including the air ambulance, paramedics, rapid response vehicle and Dorset Police.

An eyewitness also reported seeing a fire engine respond to the incident.

Concerns were first raised around 11am when cops received a call about the welfare of a man on Southbourne Cliff Drive, by Boscombe beach.

Before the man’s sad death was announced, a spokesperson for the force said: “We were called at 11.19am on Friday 26 June to a concern for welfare on Southbourne Cliff Drive near to Fisherman’s Walk.

“Officers arrived and began to engage with the man. It was subsequently reported that he has fallen from height.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A police cordon is currently in place while emergency services respond to the incident.

“We are aware there are a large number of people in the area and would ask members of the public not to share images and videos of the incident online.”

News.title: Cyclist in his 30s fighting for life after crash with ‘speeding’ unmarked police car as watchdog launches probe
News.content:
COP SMASH Cyclist in his 30s fighting for life after crash with ‘speeding’ unmarked police car as watchdog launches probe

A CYCLIST is fighting for his life in hospital after being hit by a “speeding” unmarked cop car last night.

Horrified witnesses said they “feared the worst” for the man as medics battled to save him in the road for around an hour.





Cops have confirmed the cyclist was struck by the unmarked black Volvo at around 9pm as it whizzed along Long Lane in Bermondsey, South London, while responding to an emergency call.

Witnesses at the scene said the Volvo appeared to be used by armed police officers, while the cyclist is said to have been riding a Lime bike.

One woman, who lives opposite the crash scene, told The Sun it was a “distressing” sight.

She said: “The cyclist was in a very bad way, he looked dead to be honest. It was really grim and distressing to actually see someone in that state.”



She added: “The medics were here within two minutes though, just as well Guy’s Hospital is just around the corner.

“The paramedics were doing work on him for about an hour on the road, it was very chilling really, we all felt pretty helpless.”

One passerby said that a helicopter was dispatched to take away the victim.

“I think the police, they was on a call, and then they must have been going fast, you know what it’s like when they’re on a call.



“And the cyclist must have pulled out in front of him to do a right turn.”

They said: “The helicopter landed near where I live, it’s serious if a helicopter comes, he had tubes up his nose and everything.

“They [police] was on a call, there was a cyclist… bang, that’s it…It looked like he died.

“At high speed, if you get hit by a car, if you survive, you’re lucky.”

The shaken resident said she took an elderly witness into her garden after the woman was left “hyperventilating” by what she had seen.



“I ended up taking an elderly lady who was a witness into my garden, she was in shock and like hyperventilating,” she said

“I had to calm her down, she sat in my garden for about an hour.”

A Met Police spokesperson confirmed the cyclist, a man in his 30s, was remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition.

They added that no arrests have been made, though the force says an Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) probe into the incident will be carried out.

One local said he stumbled across the aftermath of the crash while walking home from the pub.



He said: “Yesterday evening was lovely. It had been a really warm day and there was a buzz about the streets.

“That was until I walked around the corner and saw a man being given CPR in the road, which was rather sobering to say the least.

“There were lots of shocked people standing around helplessly. Everyone seemed in shock.

“Everyone stood around and said they had seen the police car speeding down the street before the impact.”

Pictures showed debris strewn across the road following the smash.



Locals told The Sun that the junction is notorious for collisions.

Grace, who works in a nearby cafe, said: “I have noticed multiple accidents here.

“I am only here two days a week and we see collisions here all the time.

“The council needs to seriously do something about it because it is chaos on this corner.

“I don’t know much about what happened last night but I have heard murmurs from customers all morning.



“It sounds really messy and I hope it isn’t as bad as we fear.”

The Met said the cyclist, a man in his 30s, remains in a life-threatening condition in hospital.

The force added that the watchdog has launched an investigation into the crash.

A Met Police spokesperson said: “At around 20:55hrs on Friday, 26 June, an unmarked police car responding to an emergency call collided with a cyclist on Long Lane, Bermondsey.

“The man on the bike, who is in his 30s, was taken to hospital where he remains in a life-threatening condition.



“No arrests have been made and the road is now clear.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As is standard practice, the Met’s Directorate of Professional Standards and the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) have been informed about the incident.

“The IOPC has begun an independent investigation and officers will continue to support them and their enquiries.”

News.title: Terrifying moment 300kg grizzly bear circles hiker walking her dog before charging at brave woman screaming ‘get away’
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a 300kg grizzly bear circles a hiker as she walks her dog.

Horrifying footage shows the huge beast charging at the woman and her pooch in a dramatic stand off, as she yells “get away”.





The woman was out walking her dog in Alberta, Canada, when the predator approached.

Video shows the bear prowling towards the hiker and her dog, but she bravely stands firm.



The woman can be heard shouting “no”, “get away” as her petrified pet stands rooted to the ground.

She then makes strange animal noises to try and scare off the beast.

Her dog faces off with the bear, slowly backing away as the predator inches closer.

The grizzly bear wanders closer before suddenly charging towards the woman and her pooch.



It chases the dog, pausing to stand on its hind legs menacingly, before continuing its pursuit.

The bear then bounds away and the hiker and her dog breathe a sigh of relief.

It retreats behind a gate and the hiker takes her chance to flee.



Experts say running is the worst thing to do when approached by a grizzly bear.

This can trigger their chase instinct – and they’re much faster than humans.

The woman backed away slowly initially instead of making a run for it.

Alberta Parks officials said: “Safety of visitors is always our top priority, and staff are monitoring the situation closely.”

They advise visitors to make loud noises and travel in groups to avoid close calls with the creatures.



Walkers should keep their dogs on leads and keep an eye out for signs the beasts have been around recently.

These include fresh digging or scat.

If a bear does approach, visitors are advised to stand their ground, and speak in a low, calm voice.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They should never scream or climb a tree to escape.

News.title: ‘Explosion’ heard as fire engine bursts into flames en route to serious crash and billows of smoke fill sky
News.content:
ENGINE INFERNO ‘Explosion’ heard as fire engine bursts into flames en route to serious crash and billows of smoke fill sky

A FIRE engine has burst into flames while en route to a road collision – with “explosions” being heard from the blazing inferno.

Emergency crews rushed to the burning vehicle on the A350 at Charlton Marshall in Dorset.





Firefighters battled to put out the fire with three hose reel jets while the vehicle’s tyres and equipment on board exploded.

One local said: “I heard sirens and a screech of tyres outside and came out of my house to see thick black smoke.

“I could see one firefighter up the road running down towards me saying telling me to go inside as there were oxygen tanks on board and it was going to blow.

“There were then a series of loud explosions with the roof of the cab of the truck blowing off into the air and landing on the pavement.”

Another resident added: “There were maybe three or four subsequent explosions and the electricity lines above the engine started to go up in flames too.

“About 20 minutes later, back up fire engines arrived and attempted to extinguish the fire.”



The crew from Blandford fire station was driving down the A-road in response to a traffic incident on June 24.

At 6.24pm, a fire erupted in the vehicle, with the driver able to stop safely.

Firefighters from Wimborne and Sturminster Newton were mobilised to the scene.

A pair of breathing apparatus wearers and multiple hose reel jets were used to put out the fire.

Locals said they could hear explosions from the fire, which were the vehicle’s tyres and cylinders onboard exploding.



The fire from the vehicle had destroyed the cab, with damage done to the nearby grass verge and telegraph cables.

Paramedics tended to the crew from the burning fire engine, with emergency personnel closing off the road.

An investigation into the incident has been launched to find out how the vehicle caught fire.

A Dorset and Wiltshire Fire and Rescue spokesperson said: “A crew from Blandford fire station was making an emergency response to a road traffic collision at 6.24pm last night (24 June) when a fire started in the fire engine while they were travelling on the A350 at Charlton Marshall.

“The crew was able to stop safely, and no-one was injured. Crews from Wimborne and Sturminster Newton were mobilised to deal with the fire, and two breathing apparatus wearers and three hose reel jets were used.



“Local residents would have heard explosions, which were the vehicle’s tyres and also cylinders on board, including breathing apparatus sets.

“An investigation into how the fire started is now underway.

“The stop came in at 8.22pm, the vehicle cab has been destroyed by fire and there was damage to the adjacent grass verge and telegraph cables.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The firefighters involved have been checked over as a precaution by paramedics, with no issues.

“The road will remain closed for some time to allow for vehicle recovery; the carriageway may need repairs, so drivers should check their route before setting off in the morning.”

News.title: Zoo where boy, 3, was ‘thrown into crocodile pit by man with learning difficulties’ reopens nine days after terror
News.content:
CROC HORROR Zoo where boy, 3, was ‘thrown into crocodile pit by man with learning difficulties’ reopens nine days after terror

Credit: Reuters

THE ZOO where a three-year-old boy was tossed into the crocodile pit has announced it is reopening after the shocking incident.

Johnsons of Old Hurst said its whole site will be open “as of this weekend”, after the boy was left in critical condition.





In a social media post today, Johnsons of Old Hurst said: “As of this weekend, our whole site will be fully open, thank you.”

It comes after the small child was allegedly thrown 15 ft into the crocodile enclosure by a man with learning difficulties last Thursday.

The boy landed on a concrete walkway, resulting in a broken arm and pelvis — and then ended up in the water.

It’s believed that the boy had been bitten by one of the crocs – either a saltwater or Nile crocodile.

He was raced to hospital with serious injuries and was in critical but stable condition.

Now, the zoo and farm where the shocking incident occurred has announced it is reopening its doors.



The 30-year-old suspect was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder but swiftly release from police custody.

Cops confirmed the man was not fit to be quizzed by officers and he has been bailed until September 18.

The announcement comes after the zoo initially said the Tropical House would be “closed until further notice” in a social media post last week.

Its statement read: “Our thoughts and prayers are with the boy and his family following the incident that occurred today.

“Out of respect to the family, our Tropical House will remain closed until further notice.”



The Johnsons added: “The rest of the site will remain open as usual.”

Yesterday, it emerged that the suspect was reportedly bundled into a car by his carers moments after the horror.

Police are now reportedly probing the two carers who were looking after the suspect during his trip to the zoo.

A source told The Telegraph that the suspect and carers left the enclosure and went to the car park after the child was thrown into the pit.

They then tried to get into a vehicle but did not leave the zoo grounds after employees intervened.



The source said: “They tried to get him into the car”.

But “another member of staff was there and prevented them from leaving” they added.

This follows reports that the carers were on their phones as the trio made their way around the zoo.

A mum, in her 20s, said: “Someone later described the man that did it and said he was with carers.

“I don’t know if it was definitely him but I saw one bloke of a bigger build, he had two carers with him and they weren’t paying him much attention.



“If it was him, his carers were maybe ten metres behind him and not paying much attention.

“They were English and chatting among themselves and on their phones.”

Cambridgeshire Police is reportedly reviewing CCTV of the incident to decide if any further action should be taken.

Tracey Johnson, who co-owns and runs the zoo, was one of the first to jump in after the child.

Her husband, Andrew clambered in after her, along with their son Edward.



The three of them bravely rescued the child, and prised him away from the grip of one of the beasts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops are currently assessing the role of the carers who were meant to be supervising the vulnerable adult during the outing.

As of Monday, the child is no longer in critical condition.

News.title: Woman who waged 15-yr war against neighbours hit with restraining order after spying & throwing dead moles over fence
News.content:
NEIGHBOUR HELL Woman who waged 15-yr war against neighbours hit with restraining order after spying & throwing dead moles over fence

A NIGHTMARE neighbour who waged a 15-year war against the couple next door has been hit with a restraining order.

Pensioner Zoi Hayes has already been hauled before the courts more than once over the bitter feud with her long-suffering neighbours Peter and Corrine Rotherham.





The pair have lived next door to each other in the Wiltshire village of Urchfont since the Rotherham’s moved into their bungalow in 2011.

The row has featured claims of spying through a hole cut in a hedge, throwing dead moles over a fence and banging a wheelie bin before dawn.

The latest clash unfolded when Hayes deliberately left a lawnmower running beside the couple’s garden while they hosted friends for a summer tapas party, a court heard.

Guests became so frustrated by the noise they went next door to ask her to switch it off.



But prosecutors said she had deliberately left the mower running to “annoy” Mrs Rotherham, putting her in breach of an existing restraining order.

Salisbury Magistrates’ Court heard the couple were entertaining six friends at a tapas party on a sunny July evening when the drama unfolded.



Prosecutor Robert Salamé said: “It was a sunny evening and at around 7.30pm the defendant parked her lawnmower directly next to the fence and she left the engine running loudly for approximately an hour.”

“It caused Corrine a degree of distress and her friends went next door to speak to Zoi.

“She admitted doing it to annoy Corrine and the matter was subsequently reported to the police as this amounted to a breach of the restraining order conditions.”

Secret footage of the incident was later used as part of a police investigation.

The latest court appearance is far from the first chapter in the remarkable neighbour war.



In 2021 Hayes was handed a five-year restraining order after damaging one of Mrs Rotherham’s sweet pea flowers.

She later breached that order and received a six-week prison sentence suspended for 12 months.

The court heard there was a “lengthy history of disputes” between the neighbours stretching back around 15 years.

Hayes admitted harassment which breached the restraining order.

She was fined £348 and ordered to pay a £139 victim surcharge and £85 in court costs.



Magistrates also imposed a fresh two-year restraining order banning her from contacting the couple or visiting their home.

The court heard Hayes has since moved from Urchfont to Dorset.

But in a statement read to the court, Mrs Rotherham said she feared Hayes could return to the area.

She said: “My concern is that she will come back to the area as she has never accepted that she has done anything wrong.

“I have heard that she is obsessed with getting revenge.”



Mrs Rotherham has previously described Hayes as a “neighbour from hell” after years of alleged harassment.

She said: “It was like living with a Peeping Tom who was absolutely obsessed with you. She cut a hole in the hedge so she could look through so we had to grow it out.

“We avoided her like the plague. It was just hell. She was a compulsive liar and a neighbour from hell.”

Representing herself, she apologised for the lawnmower incident.

Hayes said: “I would like to begin by expressing my sincere remorse for my actions and I deeply regret that incident.



“I understand that what I did was wrong and I am sorry.”

Sentencing, magistrates’ chairman Timothy Watts said: “We have listened carefully to your evidence and the prosecution.

“We noted your remorse but we also noted your relevant convictions.

“We have decided to deal with this with a fine. A restraining order will be put in place for two years.”

But after sentence was passed, Hayes launched one final broadside at her long-time rival.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “You have to remember that there are two sides to every story.

“She finds a way to twist everything. I will only be happy when she takes her last breath.”

News.title: Home Secretary blasted over new ‘open borders’ scheme to allow thousands of refugees into UK legally
News.content:
NEW ROUTES Home Secretary blasted over new ‘open borders’ scheme to allow thousands of refugees into UK legally

Credit: PA

THOUSANDS of refugees will be brought to the UK under a new scheme set to be launched by the Home Secretary next week.

Political opponents slammed the Government for the “open borders” plan, arguing there needs to be a crackdown on illegal immigration first.





Shabana Mahmood is expected to announce “capped safe and legal” routes to the UK in a bid to crack down on small boat migrants.

Applications for the new community sponsorship scheme will open this autumn, according to The Times.

More than 10,000 refugees are hoped to be brought into the country in the next decade under the new resettlement scheme.

Tory shadow home secretary Chris Philp blasted the plans, arguing “it won’t stop the boats”.



Philp said: “75,000 illegal immigrants have entered the UK in the last two years.

“Until this is zero, we shouldn’t be shipping any extra people in at all on ‘humanitarian’ grounds.



“Unless every person that wants to come is let in (which would be mad) it won’t stop the boats.

“Open borders Labour revealing their true colours again.”

So far this year, more than 11,000 migrants have crossed the Channel in small boats.

The figure for 2026 so far is almost 40 per cent down compared to this time last year.

The Liberal Democrats also agreed more needed to be done to stop small boat arrivals.



But Max Wilkinson, Liberal Democrat home affairs spokesman, said the new scheme was a “step in the right direction”.

Mahmood said the new route would allow in “genuine refugees” and “close loopholes that have too often been abused”.

It will allow universities and other approved organisations to “sponsor” refugees to come and live in the UK after undergoing background checks.

“Britain has always offered sanctuary to those fleeing war and persecution,” Mahmood told the BBC.

Due to be announced in the government’s Immigration and Asylum Bill on Tuesday, it is regarded as an attempt by Mahmood to win over the left flank of the Labour Party.



The bill also contains controversial legislation cracking down on the asylum appeal system.

This includes reforms to human rights and modern slavery laws to make it easier for the Home Office to reject “vexatious” asylum claims.

She has already ended permanent refugee status, replacing it with temporary protections.

While the Home Secretary is expected to keep her job if Burnham becomes leader, she has faced criticism within the party for her strict asylum policies.

The new route is intended to help refugees who are fleeing conflict and natural disasters in their home country.



Another route, which would allow refugees to be sponsored by employers, is set to be rolled out next year.

It is thought the Home Office will cap the number of arrivals under the scheme, but it is not known how many that might be.

The reforms are understood to be based on the Canadian scheme, which allows people to “sponsor” refugees by pledging to provide support, including finances, for a year after they arrive.

This is similar to the Homes for Ukraine scheme which saw 200,000 Ukrainians sponsored to come to the UK on temporary visas.

While this was seen as a successful project, the Home Secretary reportedly hopes her new scheme will replace these “ad hoc” programmes for specific countries.



It comes as the Home Office has sunk into all-out farce with Mahmood banning her own immigration minister from viewing official documents.

She imposed the extraordinary restriction on Mike Tapp after Starmer refused to fire him for writing an article in The Times to publicly argue foreign care workers should be spared Labour’s tougher settlement rules.

He wrote it was his “strong belief” foreign care workers who had “played by the rules” should not face Labour’s planned extension of the wait for indefinite leave to remain from five years to ten.

He will stay in post but cannot view Home Office papers or hold official meetings without approval.

Mahmood was unaware of the article before it was published and asked Sir Keir to sack him for a Ministerial Code breach.



But No 10 made it clear that the final decision rested with the PM.

A spokesman said: “It is not for any individual Secretary of State to determine whether the Ministerial Code has been followed, it is a matter for the PM alone.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Earlier, Tapp insisted on social media: “I won’t be intimidated to drop my views. Stay classy!”

The row triggered a backlash inside Labour, with one Government aide branding Mahmood “completely shameless and dishonourable”.

News.title: ‘Organise kitchen cupboards’ for £2 with Home Bargains ‘convenient’ household item
News.content:
‘Organise kitchen cupboards’ for £2 with Home Bargains ‘convenient’ household item

The high street retailer claims the item is the 'perfect storage solution'

View 3 Images Take a look at the latest deal at Home Bargains (Image: Home Bargains)

Shoppers looking to make the most of their kitchen cupboards could do just that with an item now on sale at Home Bargains. The discount retailer, renowned for its extensive collection of homeware and furniture bargains, professes it is the "perfect storage solution".

‌



Home Bargains boasts over 600 locations across the UK, each one selling everything from side tables and wardrobes to garden essentials, and even beauty products like shampoo and moisturiser. It also continues to add to its range of storage options, and the latest deal could be the pick of the bunch.

‌



The Diamond Storage with Lid 3.5L comes in four different colours - cream, green, grey and pink - and retails for £1.99. Demand is so high that at the time of publication, only green and grey remain in stock, so interested buyers are urged to grab one while stocks last.

‌



Describing the product online, Home Bargains said: "Keep your space tidy with the Diamond 3.5L Storage with Lid! Perfect for stashing away toys or tech, these handy baskets come with carry handles for easy transport and a sleek design that fits any room.

"Whether storing away old toys, new technology or organising the kitchen cupboards, these storage baskets with lids are the perfect storage solution! The convenient carry handles are ideal for moving goods from one room to another."

It features a textured woven-effect design on the outside, integrated carry handles on either side, and can be used to organise household items like toiletries, cleaning products, toys, stationary or clothing.

Home Bargains offers standard UK delivery for £3.95, or for free on orders over £100, with delivery normally taking about four days. The store sells a wide range of other possible storage solutions too. Take the Home Solutions Storage Box 9L, for example, which retails for £2.99.

Article continues below

View 3 Images The Home Solutions Storage Box at Home Bargains (Image: Home Bargains)

"Get your space sorted with the Home Solutions Storage Box," reads the product description on the Home Bargains website. "This 9-litre, BPA-free wonder is perfect for decluttering your kitchen, organising your closet, or tidying up a playroom - keeping everything neat and easily accessible!"

Made from clear plastic, the storage box has a translucent body, a matching lid and two blue clip-lock handles. It is suitable for storing everyday household items such as clothes, toys and documents.

News.title: EE mobile customers given £4.27 'payment reminder' warning
News.content:
EE mobile customers given £4.27 'payment reminder' warning

People with the mobile phone netwrok have been made aware of the email

View 3 Images Millions of people are with the mobile phone network (Image: Getty)

People with the mobile phone network EE have been issued a warning over a 'payment reminder'. EE Limited, formerly known as Everything Everywhere Limited, is a mobile network operator and internet service provider based in the UK.

‌



It is part of BT Consumer, a branch of BT Group. Founded in 2010, it has grown into the UK's third-largest mobile network operator, with 21.2 million customers. With millions of users, people are being alerted to e mails claiming to be from 'EE'.

‌



In a new alert issued by the Norfolk Trading Standards, a warning has gone out to EE customers about emails circulating. These emails are claiming to be a 'Payment Reminder' as 'your last bill payment was not settled in full and there remains an outstanding balance of £4.27 on your account'.

‌



The email goes on to state that 'to avoid any potential service interruption' payment should be made via a link included in the text. However, these emails are fake, and anyone following the link will be taken to a fake version of the EE website, which will attempt to gather personal, account and financial details or download malware onto your device.

The organisation says: "The criminals sending these emails often use small amounts as the figure to be paid as they believe people are more likely to make payment to avoid issues with their service but would question requests for larger amounts.

View 3 Images The email is a scam

‌



"Our advice is always to be wary of claims made in unexpected email approaches and never click on links or open attachments if approached in this way. It is highly likely that versions of this email will be circulating claiming different outstanding amounts."

If you have concerns regarding the security of your online account, always log in directly through the official website or app. Alternatively, you can contact your service provider's customer service using a number from a recent bill, their official website, or the app. Never use contact numbers that are included in these emails.

You can report any suspicious email received by forwarding it to report@phishing.gov.uk. You can also report scams received to us via our partners, the Citizens Advice consumer helpline on freephone 0808 223 1133.

Article continues below

View 3 Images EE says it won't ask for your PIN or password by text or email

On the EE website, it offers information on how to spot scams and what steps to take. EE says: "We'll never ask you for your PIN or password by text or email."

It adds: "Don’t click on links unless you’re 100% sure they are genuine. Take a moment to stop and think and trust your instincts. If it looks too good to be true or looks suspicious, there’s probably a catch. Don’t give away any of your personal details or give anyone access to your computer or mobile – if you think you might have provided your bank account details, contact your bank immediately."

News.title: Inside Britain's 'boom' in Chinese cars as showrooms ditch Western brands and Iran war sends drivers electric
News.content:
Inside Britain's 'boom' in Chinese cars as showrooms ditch Western brands and Iran war sends drivers electric

EXCLUSIVE: Hundreds of car showrooms across Britain are ditching traditional European and US brands in favour of Chinese challengers as experts and motorists explain why new names are appearing on UK roads

View 9 Images Britain is now one of the largest markets for Chinese cars (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

British drivers and car showrooms are abandoning well-known Western brands for Chinese rivals as the Iran war petrol crisis accelerates the shift towards electric cars.

‌



Over the past two years, hundreds of dealerships across the nation have been refitted to house a new wave of Beijing-backed car brands - such as Jaecoo, XPENG, Chery, Changan, and Omoda. BYD, already the UK's best-selling EV brand, says it wants to be the nation's number one overall within the next five years - and has reported 113% growth in 2026 so far compared to the year before.

‌



Even MG, a quintessentially British car marque, is now a fully owned subsidiary of Shanghai-headquartered SAIC Motors. The shift towards Chinese vehicles comes as data shows the hybrid Jaecoo 7 battling it out for the UK's best selling car of 2026. It's currently in third and ahead of some established names, such as the Vauxhall Corsa, Ranger Rover Sport and the Mini Cooper.

‌



Anti-electric car Donald Trump sparks boom in UK EV sales over Iran war petrol price rises READ MORE :

Gen Z ditching cars for Uber and e-bikes as half of young Brits have no plans to learn to drive READ MORE :

View 9 Images An ex-Ford dealership in Rotherham before its conversion

Last month was the best May for overall car sales in Britain since the pandemic, with EVs from China leading the charge. The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT), who put together the figures, said 27.3% of all new sales were electric, putting the boom down to "increasingly competitive offers" amid "economic and geopolitical uncertainty".

Taking full advantage of this trend are bosses at major UK car retailers, with at least 300 showrooms estimated to have been set up for Chinese EVs and hybrids over the past 24 months. The majority of these are existing sites that have shifted away from Western brands, which in contrast are actively scaling back their physical sales presence.

‌



View 9 Images And after becoming a BYD showroom

Evans Halshaw rebranded at least five sites - including Ford locations in Rotherham and Bury - into BYD showrooms, while London-based Ancaster Group has completely repurposed its Hyundai forecourt in Welling, London to launch Omoda and Jaecoo.

Vertu Motors converted some of its traditional Ford premises, such as its Hartlepool branch, into dedicated BYD hubs, and the 78-year-old Yorkshire family business JCT600 recently cleared out its Volkswagen Vans site at Priory Tec Park in Hessle, near Hull, to house Changan.

‌



Steve Fowler, a motoring expert who has served as a judge for the World Car of the Year awards, told the Mirror: "These Chinese brands are looking after their dealers better than some of the established brands have been... they are looking after their dealers really well.

View 9 Images The Jaecoo 7 is one of the UK's best-selling cars of the year so far (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

"And they're looking after their customers better because they’re incentivised to do so.

‌



"A Chinese car has to be explained a little bit more, the consumer is is a little bit more wary about them. You’ve got to try harder to sell them. And I think that’s what people are liking, the fact that the dealership is is working harder to explain the cars to answer all the questions, which, frankly, the established legacy players are not doing, and they haven’t been doing for years."

View 9 Images Sandra Wilkinson, 61, with her 88-year-old mother Eileen Jones and her 96-year-old ex-Mirror reporter father Reginald Jones (Image: Sandra Wilkinson)

Sandra Wilkinson, 61, looks after her 88-year-old mother Eileen Jones and her 96-year-old ex-Mirror reporter father Reginald Jones at home in Bramhall, Cheshire. She said her Jaecoo 7 4x4 hybrid helps them get out and about in the countryside for lunch and afternoon tea, and is also useful for trips to North Wales and the Scottish Highlands.

‌



She explained: "They've made it a hard car not to buy, and I think that European and North American car manufacturers have got a hell of a competitor on their hands."

"I was looking for a car that I could transport two elderly parents comfortably, and that they could get in and out of very easily. It’s not a sports car, it doesn’t feel like it’s stuck to the road. But it's a very comfortable ride that is incredible value for money."

"It ticked every box. Did I worry about the fact that it was Chinese and it was new? I think I was a bit worried that maybe the parts might not be available, but once they start manufacturing them here... no more problem."

‌



View 9 Images This old Ford showroom in Hartlepool is being rebranded to reflect new BYD branding

Reginald, whose big stories included during his 35-year career included the Moors Murders and a 17-day police stand-off in Shropshire, added: "The car does the job... and I couldn't care less who makes it!"

Taxi driver Rob Dunkerley, 56, from Fleet, Hampshire, has been using Jaecoo model for six months after previously driving his passengers around in a Toyota Avensis - and was "very pleased with the car so far". "The only downside for me is the boot isn’t as big as I’d like", he added.

‌



View 9 Images Taxi driver Rob Dunkerley with his Jaecoo 7 (Image: Rob Dunkerley)

Tu Pham, a BMW driver of 25 years, told us that his family had already made the move to BYD - and he was now looking at an XPeng too. China's car exports not always been warmly received, with their reputation for failing crash dummy tests making them the butt of jokes on Top Gear as recently as the early 2010s.

But that perception may now be shifting thanks to some long-term strategic thinking in Beijing, which has seen Chinese manufacturers "leap frog" Western competitors by switching development to EVs early. More recently, Donald Trump's war in Iran has sent prices at the pump soaring, pushing previously sceptical drivers towards EVs for their next purchase.

‌



View 9 Images Professor David Bailey said the 'Brexit effect' means the UK has lower tariffs on Chinese cars than the EU and US (Image: © ALEX ROACHE)

Professor David Bailey from Birmingham Business School explained that the "Brexit effect" means the UK has significantly lower tariffs than the EU and the US, making this country a "target" for Chinese manufacturers.

He said: "The US has got tariffs of more than 100% on Chinese EVs, which is keeping lots of them out. The European Union has various tariffs of up to about 45% for some Chinese brands... but the UK doesn't have that tariff. We have just a simple standard 10% tariff. So because of that Chinese brands are very much targeting the UK because it's wide open for them.

‌



"Because the Chinese market has essentially stagnated because of slow economic growth and various other things, the government's industrial strategies are very much shifted towards exports and exports of EVs in particular - and the UK is a major market for this."

He said the rate of growth could eventually raise questions over whether tariffs should be introduced - but that "if you want people to get into EVs, then it's going to be cheap Chinese EVs that will do that much more quickly."

View 9 Images Nissan's Sunderland factory is set to build Chery cars in a historic first (Image: PA)

Article continues below

Last month, Nissan announced plans to build Chery passenger vehicles at its Sunderland factory - securing the future of its 6,000-strong workforce, and marking the first time a Chinese manufacturer would make its cars in Britain should it go ahead.

Experts believe it's a sign that China's hand in the car industry is set to only strengthen over the coming years. Professor Bailey added: "You've got this situation where, because the European industry including the UK is under so much pressure, they've got a lot of spare capacity. And so companies are looking to bring in Chinese players to build in that spare capacity - including Stellantis with Leapmotor, Nissan with Chery.

"We may see further moves. JLR has got a lot of spare capacity and in fact with Chery they've got a kind of joint venture to make the Freelander model, which I think is eventually becoming a separate brand."

News.title: UK weather maps show new scorching heatwave within days as 17 counties hit 38C
News.content:
UK weather maps show new scorching heatwave within days as 17 counties hit 38C

Temperatures in the UK should start cooling off tomorrow following a scorching heatwave this week, but forecasting maps show another heat surge could be just days away from bringing 38C

View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 8 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Another scorching heatwave could be just days away from sending temperatures in the UK surging to 38C, weather forecasting maps show.

‌



Yesterday was the hottest day of the year so far - and the hottest June day in history - as a heatwave which has been roasting Brits all week saw 37.3C recorded in Santon Downham.

‌



The Met Office had been forced to issue rarely-seen red weather warnings for extreme heat in England. The heatwave has also brought thunderstorms and lightning, which has caused significant damage to buildings in some areas.

‌



The Met Office’s latest forecast suggests peak temperature will finally drop back below 30C tomorrow. However, it might not be too long before the 30C mark is breached once again.

View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 9 (Image: WXCHARTS)

UK weather maps show 54 counties plunging below 10C as heatwave ends – full list READ MORE :

The GFS weather model suggests a four-day heatwave is on the cards at the start of next month, starting on July 8. The data shows highs of 30C to 33C right across central and southern England on July 8, with the warmest temperatures coming in western areas as well as the south-east.

‌



For July 9, the maps show temperatures rising as high as 36C close to London, with 35C coming quite widely across southern and eastern England. Parts of Wales are also expected to reach 30C.

View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 10 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Scorching 38C highs are expected to follow on July 10, the GFS weather model suggests, with western England and the south seeing the hottest conditions. Most of England and Wales is shown on the maps as peaking at more than 30C.

‌



And temperatures could again reach 38C on July 11, in the north-west, Midlands, Yorkshire and the south-east. Areas as far north as the England-Scotland border could see highs of 30C or more, the data suggests.

View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on July 11 (Image: WXCHARTS)

Temperature anomaly maps for this period show the UK shaded in deep red, particularly England. This shows where temperatures are expected to surge well above the seasonal average.

‌



In total, the GFS weather model maps show 17 counties could reach 38C or more. They are all in England.

Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office says “hot” conditions could develop in July, with a risk of some “thundery showers”. Its forecast for July 11 to 25 states: “High pressure patterns are looking slightly more likely than low pressure patterns during the early part of this period, meaning a greater chance of settled and drier than average conditions.

“Although with outbreaks of rain and stronger winds at times, more especially across the north. There is still a chance of some changeable or more unsettled conditions developing later in the period, with a risk of some heavy and thundery showers. Temperatures are likely to be above normal on the whole, with a greater than normal chance of hot conditions developing at times.”

News.title: Gen Z ditching cars for Uber and e-bikes as half of young Brits have no plans to learn to drive
News.content:
Gen Z ditching cars for Uber and e-bikes as half of young Brits have no plans to learn to drive

Energy firm Hive commissioned the poll of 2,000 Brits aged 18-30 to highlight greener travel during London Climate Action Week and it found that Gen Z take a very different view on driving

View 3 Images Getting your first car, as depicted in cult comedy The Inbetweeners, has long been seen as a rite of passage, but Gen Z-ers say it no longer is (Image: Channel 4)

Forget having a Ford Fiesta as your first banger - Gen Z would rather book an Uber.

‌



Half of young Brits (50%) have no plans to ever learn to drive, while the same number reckon they can happily live without owning a car. For generations, passing your test meant freedom, independence and finally ditching Mum and Dad's lifts. But today's twentysomethings are swerving the milestone altogether.

‌



A whopping 77% think driving is becoming less important, while 71% say it's no longer the rite of passage it used to be. Some 29% of youngsters say they're too scared to get behind the wheel, while soaring fuel prices put off one in four.

‌



View 3 Images Taxi apps like Uber are popular among Gen Z, who would rather use them than drive their own car (Image: PA)

Top ways men are taking care of themselves - take our online quiz to check how healthy you are READ MORE :

Workers born between these two years enjoy pay boost READ MORE :

Among Gen Z city dwellers, 68% say owning a car is no longer an important life goal, while 79% would rather spend their money on holidays, brunches or dating. Instead of splashing out on a battered hatchback, they're tapping for ride-shares, e-bikes and trains.

London tops the UK's car-free league table, with 61% of adults saying they don't drive, ahead of Liverpool and Plymouth. More than half (58%) say owning a car in a city is basically pointless thanks to public transport, cycling and ride-hailing apps.

‌



Meanwhile, more than a third (35%) see cars as a money pit, 33% simply can't afford one, while 31% say driving lessons and insurance are both too expensive. Going green is another major factor.

And nearly nine in ten (87%) Gen Z-ers say environmental concerns influence every transport choice they make - far higher than among the over-30s. Moreover, seven in ten actively choose electric or low-emission taxis whenever possible, while almost two-thirds of those who do want a licence say they'd only learn in an EV.

View 3 Images The findings come as Hive shines a spotlight on greener travel during London Climate Action Week, with its Hive Taxi appearing outside Battersea Power Station (Image: Andrew Hasson)

Article continues below

Gen Z refers to people born between 1997 and 2012. They follow Millennials, born 1981–1996, and precede Gen Alpha, born 2013 onward.

Energy firm Hive commissioned the poll of 2,000 Brits aged 18-30 to highlight greener travel during London Climate Action Week, with its Hive Taxi appearing around the capital. Tom Pakenham, Commercial Director for Hive, said: "It's encouraging to see how people of all ages are embracing greener ways to travel.

"Electric vehicles are no longer a niche choice - they're becoming the future. As more people look to travel sustainably, we're proud to support that shift through EV charging and smarter energy solutions."

News.title: Popular Swedish food chain to open UK restaurants as recruitment drive launched
News.content:
Popular Swedish food chain to open UK restaurants as recruitment drive launched

Fast-growing Swedish food chain Holy Greens describes its concept as 'Scandinavian mindful eating' and is set to open its first restaurants in the UK

View 3 Images Holy Greens is opening a site in Canary Wharf (Image: Jam Press/Holy Greens)

A popular Swedish food chain is set to launch in the UK with several new restaurants planned.

‌



Holy Greens, which specialises in fresh salads, warm bowls and healthy meals, will make its British debut this summer with a site at Cabot Square in London's Canary Wharf.

‌



The company, which operates around 30 restaurants across Sweden, describes its concept as "Scandinavian mindful eating", with a focus on health, sustainability and conscious living.

‌



On its website, Holy Greens says its community is built around shared values, adding: "Our guests are more than customers; they are ambassadors of a lifestyle." The chain also says it wants to build "a strong connection with individuals who care about what they eat and its impact on the world around them, without being overly complicated".

View 3 Images The company operates around 30 restaurants across Sweden (Image: Jam Press/Holy Greens)

US fast food chain where diners sign waiver set to open 50 restaurants in UK READ MORE :

Alongside the first restaurant, Holy Greens is already planning several more London openings and has begun recruiting staff. Advertising the expansion, the company says: "Be part of our Scandinavian community. We are planning several new openings around London in the coming years and are always looking for new employees who respect people's differences and are passionate about providing good service. Join our green revolution."

‌



Founded in 2013 by David Egonson and Nebojsa Pavicevic and headquartered in Malmö, Holy Greens is backed by investment firm Equip Capital.

Chief executive Sabrina Jaeger said: "This marks an important step in our international journey, but it is also the result of nearly two years of focused work across the entire organisation.

"International expansion is often viewed as a single strategic decision. The reality is very different. It involves countless analyses, market visits, pilot runs, refinements to our unit economics, supplier negotiations and building the right organisational capabilities.

‌



View 3 Images The restaurant describes its concept as 'Scandinavian mindful eating' (Image: Jam Press/Holy Greens)

"We have deliberately taken the time to ensure that the foundation is strong: both operationally and culturally. London is one of Europe's most competitive food markets. Entering a market like this requires discipline, resilience and a clear point of differentiation.

"We do so with great respect for the market, but also with confidence in our concept, our brand and the results we have consistently delivered across Sweden so far.

Article continues below

"Expanding into new markets is never just about strategy and numbers. It is about people, culture and the ability to execute together over a long period of time.

"London is our first step beyond Scandinavia. Our ambition extends much further, and we are building for the long term. The foundation is in place. Now, the next chapter begins."

News.title: Strawberry Moon: Where to see it, what is it, and how it got its name
News.content:
Strawberry Moon: Where to see it, what is it, and how it got its name

The stunning Strawberry Moon will be visible in the sky on June 30 - but it might be a little bit of a challenge to find a spot to see it

View 3 Images A 'Strawberry' Moon rises over Burr Wood in Derbyshire in 2016 (Image: SWNS)

In a few days time a coppery, crimson full moon appear in the sky, dubbed with the whimsical name as the Strawberry Moon.

‌



The Strawberry full moon, the seventh of this year because of the unusual Blue Moon that appeared in May, will appear low in our skies - but that could make it hard to get a good look at the stunning display. It will begin to rise on Monday June 29 and it is expected to peak around 12.57am on June 30, but depending on whereabouts you are in the country, the peak will occur at slightly different times. However, tonight (Saturday 27 June) it will rise close to a red star, called the 'scorpion's heart', promising a gorgeous view.

‌



Last year saw the strongest sighting of the Strawberry Moon we will be blessed with for a long time - it won't be until 2043 that the Strawberry Moon sat that low on the horizon again, because of the years-long cycle the moon orbits. However, the 2026 Strawberry full moon still promises a unique view for stargazers as the lunar display takes on a pinky, dusky hue.

‌



The Mirror breaks down everything you need to know about the upcoming Strawberry Moon...

Where to see the Strawberry Moon?

Tonight, the Moon will be close to the Antares star, which is the brightest star in the constellation of Scorpio, which is why this star is known as 'scorpion heart'. It will be positioned to the left of the star, to see the lunar and star display, you will need to look low down in the Southern sky.

This year's strawberry moon is a micromoon, this is because its at the farthest stage away from the Earth in its orbit, so it will look smaller in the sky and not appear squashed, like it isn't quite a full circle. However, because the Strawberry Moon appears so low in the sky, close to the horizon it will still look bigger than usual.

‌



View 3 Images The Strawberry Moon sits low on the horizon (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

To take in the full moon on Monday, it will start to rise at sunset but be most visible late in the evening, peaking at 12.57pm, per the Royal Observatory Greenwich, although as mentioned above it could vary depending on your location across the country. You should position yourself with a clear south-easterly view, ideally with as few blockages as possible along the horizon.

Why is it called the Strawberry Moon?

Normally the sixth full moon of the year, the June full moon is commonly dubbed the Strawberry Moon. The name is said to come from North America, where it rose in the sky at the same time as the first harvests of strawberries, originating with the Native Americans and Algonquin and brought back to the UK as a moniker by colonists.

‌



However, some historic European names for the moon are similar. It's often dubbed the Rose Moon and sometimes it's called the Honey Moon and the Mead Moon as well. Others have called it the hot moon, because it occurs at the start of the warmest period of the year.

Why is the Strawberry Moon a different colour?

Most often, the Strawberry Moon appears orange, or coppery coloured, but occasionally it appears with pinky hues. Whilst it would be romantic to assume this has something to do with why it is called the Strawberry Moon, unfortunately that isn't the case, it's do with the science behind its positioning.

First up there is Rayleigh scattering. Because the moon will be low on the horizon, the light must travel through much more of the Earth's atmosphere. Molecules of nitrogen, oxygen, as well as tiny aerosols in the air make short-wavelength light (violet, blue, green) scatter, but they do this less efficiently with long-wavelength light (orange, red). The longer the light's journey through that haze, the more of the blues are stripped away, which means that it's primarily the reds and oranges that manage to reach our eyes, giving off the rusty, coppery hue.

‌



View 3 Images Full Strawberry Moon

Secondly, it's pollution, dust and smoke that strip more and more of the blue, green and violet, short wavelength light away, adding to the appearance that the moon is a reddish orange. Once again, because the moon is closer and sitting low on the horizon, the light has to pass through these pollutants and dust, as well as water vapour, which are larger particles that selectively absorb and scatter light.

What are the names of all the full moons?

Every full moon has its own nickname, not just the Strawberry Moon. Below is a full list of the all the nicknames bestowed upon full moons throughout 2026.

‌



January – Wolf Moon

February – Snow Moon

March - Worm Moon

‌



April – Pink Moon

May – Flower Moon

Second May Full Moon - Blue Moon

‌



June – Strawberry Moon

July – Buck Moon

August – Sturgeon Moon

‌



September – Corn Moon

October – Hunter's Moon

November – Beaver Moon

Article continues below

December – Cold Moon

News.title: People are just realising why washing up liquid is green
News.content:
People are just realising why washing up liquid is green

'It contains no green active ingredients'

View Image Many washing up liquids are green as a default colour (Image: Getty)

People are just realising why many washing up liquids are green - and the reason may surprise you.

‌



Annabel Port, curator at The Other British Museum, regularly takes to social media to discuss the modern day items which symbolise modern Britain. And in a recent post she explained why the 'default' colour of washing up liquid is green. It's all to do with the first washing up liquid in the UK - Fairy - which was made available to consumers back in 1959.

‌



Explaining the colour, Annabel said: "The first British washing up liquid was Fairy in 1959, and they've always made a big deal about it being green. Did we really need the colour in 'mild green Fairy liquid'?"

‌



Later, other brands brought out their own versions and these were also green - "like it was the rule". Annabel continued: "But it contains no green active ingredients. It's been dyed this colour, so why green?

"Back in 1898 Fairy soap was launched and was used for everything. Clothes, dishes, skin, whatever. It was made in Newcastle by Thomas Hedley and Co and early ads show that the soap was also green - olive green, and for a reason - it contained olive oil."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

There is no longer olive oil in Fairy, but "this was their brand colour and they stuck with it and other companies blindly followed. Fairy liquid was a trailblazer".

Many people have rushed to the post's comments section to share their thoughts. One Instagram user wrote: "Who knew that Newcastle was the home of Fairy liquid?"

Article continues below

A second said: "My Mum always had a cake of Fairy soap for washing clothes by hand. I didn’t know about the olive oil though." A third added: "Brilliant. I didn't realise the olive oil connection."

A fourth wrote: "1959 seems late for washing up liquid in the realm of inventions. And also it’s weird how other colours doesn’t look quite right."
